_meta.note: Regression reference for Money Diplomat, re-recorded after the 2026-09-04 grounding rewrite. The v1 golden was discarded: its expected output carried confidence percentages, resentment_risk, culture_clash_risk, the_real_issue, emotional_stakes, if_guilt_trip, what_splitting_signals, likely_outcome and likely_counteroffer — every one of which the new schemas removed. The money-profile and monthly-recap endpoints are gone entirely and their cases with them. Re-run with `npm run check:golden money-diplomat`. The north star, and what to read for by eye: the tool is strongest answering 'what is fair or prudent here, given what I actually know, and what can I say?' and weakest answering 'what is this person secretly thinking?', 'what will happen?', 'what does my culture require?' or 'what number is objectively correct?'. Reason about the money, help with the conversation, do not invent the people. Each case carries its own `guards` line. See audit/tool-notes/MONEYDIPLOMAT-NOTES.md.

cases.name: lend-overdue-first-loan
cases.guards: The case in the owner's PDF. The first loan is overdue and undiscussed; that is the strongest supplied fact and the whole answer rests on it. NOTHING may predict repayment, forecast resentment, or say the friendship will suffer. The holiday appears as a bare fact in what_is_known and is never read as evidence of ability, priorities or willingness. Plus the seven from the final micro-pass: an overdue undiscussed loan does NOT mean there is no shared understanding of whether it is still owed — the agreement was already established, so silence is not doubt. what_is_not_known holds exactly three kinds of thing and none of them is the other person's inner life: why it has not been repaid or discussed, what is being asked for now, and the LENDER's own financial position — not what the friend believes, intends or expects. before_you_decide must not propose a history the visitor contradicted (no 'or does your friend believe it was settled'), and frames the money constraint as what could be UNAVAILABLE if repayment is delayed, never what could be written off — the second quietly reclassifies a loan as money to expect to lose. No prediction of how a conversation will feel. terms_to_clarify must not demand a missed-date clause as though a loan between friends were a contract. And the refusal script may not assert the borrower's circumstances: 'I understand you are asking for help' is grounded, 'I understand you are in a tight spot' is not. recommendation is pinned English because the frontend colours on it.

input.situation: A friend is asking to borrow $400. I lent them $600 about eight months ago which was supposed to be paid back within three months and never was. We have not talked about it since. They just posted about booking a holiday.
input.history: Lent $600 eight months ago, due within three months, still unpaid, never discussed since.

why: An existing $600 loan is five months overdue and has not been discussed, so the first loan is unresolved before a second is requested.
Adding $400 would bring total unpaid lending to $1,000 with no agreed repayment conversation on record.
Raising the earlier loan first is a reasonable step before deciding on the new request.
what_is_known: You lent $600 approximately eight months ago, due within three months.
The original repayment date passed without repayment and the loan has not been discussed since.
Your friend is now asking to borrow $400.
Your friend recently posted about booking a holiday.
what_is_not_known: Why the $600 has not been repaid or raised.
What specifically the $400 is needed for and on what repayment terms.
Your own financial position and what amount you could afford to have unavailable if repayment is delayed.
before_you_decide: What happened with the original $600 repayment agreement, and what can your friend realistically do about it now?
What amount could you afford to have unavailable if repayment of either loan is delayed?
Are you comfortable raising the earlier loan before giving an answer on the new request?

if_you_lend.amount_guidance: If you decide to lend after the earlier loan has been addressed, consider an amount you could afford to have unavailable for an extended period. Lending an additional $400 while $600 is outstanding would leave $1,000 unresolved.
terms_to_clarify: Acknowledge the existing $600 openly and agree what happens with it before any new money moves.
Agree on a specific repayment date for the new amount.
If repayment timing matters to you, agree out loud what you will both do if circumstances change.
if_you_lend.script: Hey, I want to help where I can, but before I answer on the $400 I need to talk about the $600 from earlier in the year. Can we sort out what the plan is for that first? Once we have that conversation I am happy to think about the new request with you.

if_you_do_not_lend.script: I understand you are asking for help, but I have to say no to lending more right now. I also think we need to catch up about the $600 from earlier — it has been sitting unaddressed for a while and I would like to talk through it.
if_you_do_not_lend.if_they_push: My answer on lending more is no for now. I do still want to sort out where we stand on the earlier amount.

existing_debt.next_step: Raise the $600 directly before responding to the new request. A low-key, factual opening works better than an accusation.
existing_debt.script: I wanted to bring something up — the $600 I lent you back in January was due a few months ago and we have not talked about it since. I am not angry, I just want to know where things stand. What is the plan for paying that back?

cases.name: venmo-three-weeks
cases.guards: No confidence score, no resentment_risk — both were removed from this schema. The verdict is pinned English. Nothing may predict whether asking damages the relationship.

input.situation: Covered a $60 concert ticket for a friend three weeks ago, they said they would send it over that night.

why: There was a clear, specific agreement: payment that same night — so this is not an ambiguous loan.
Three weeks have passed with no mention of the missed commitment, which means a follow-up is overdue by the terms they both set.
$60 is a real amount that most people would expect to follow through on.
what_matters: The explicit same-night promise makes this a broken commitment, not a forgotten favor.
Whether any contact has happened since — if there has been none, a casual message is the natural next step.
Whether the friend acknowledged it at all after the concert.
unknowns: Whether the friend sent a message since that the user did not mention — that would change the tone needed.
Whether the friend is going through something that made them lose track — not assumed, but worth keeping in mind when reading the reply.
output.script: Hey — just a heads up, that $60 for the concert ticket never came through. No big deal, just want to sort it out. Can you send it over when you get a chance?
output.if_they_push_back: Totally fine if timing is tight — just let me know when works. You did say that night, so I wanted to make sure it did not slip through the cracks.

cases.name: afford-sparse-numbers
cases.guards: Cost and income only. gut_check must NOT be 'Looks manageable' on this alone — what_is_missing should be substantial, because cost and income are insufficient for a real affordability answer. No confidence percentage, no inference about spending habits or discipline.

what_the_numbers_show: $1,800 is roughly 53% of one month's take-home pay.
No other figures were supplied, so no further arithmetic is possible.
what_is_missing: Monthly fixed expenses (rent, utilities, debt payments, etc.).
Current savings or any dedicated holiday fund.
Whether the $1,800 would be paid at once or spread over time.
Any upcoming costs that compete for the same money.
questions_to_check: After all your regular monthly bills, how much is typically left over?
Could you cover this without touching an emergency fund or going into debt?
Is there a payment deadline, or time to save toward it gradually?
Would paying this leave you short for any known expense in the next few months?
output.low_regret_next_step: Write out your fixed monthly outgoings and subtract them from $3,400 before deciding. If the remainder covers $1,800 without drawing down savings you need as a buffer, the numbers may work — but that step has to come first.

cases.name: tip-unverified-norm
cases.guards: Arithmetic from the supplied bill only. The local norm is NOT verified, so it belongs in check_first, not asserted in practical_answer. No invented service charge, auto-gratuity or party-size rule.

input.situation: Dinner out, service was slow but friendly

output.practical_answer: Tipping norms in Portugal vary and are not settled enough to name a standard percentage here — see check_first before deciding. If you want a starting point while you verify: rounding up or leaving a small amount (roughly 5-10%) is one approach some visitors use, but this should not be treated as an established local norm.

math.percentage_used: 5% and 10% shown as a range only — these are illustrative, not verified local norms

why: Service was slow, which some people weigh as a reason to tip toward the lower end of whatever range applies
Service was friendly, which some people weigh as a reason not to go to zero even when pace was off
Party of 4 — worth checking whether an automatic gratuity was already included on the bill
check_first: Local tipping expectations vary; check the current norm for restaurant tipping in Portugal before settling on an amount
Review the printed bill for any service charge or gratuity line — if one is already included, adding more is your choice, not an obligation
Some Portuguese restaurants add a cover charge (couvert) for bread and appetizers placed on the table — confirm whether that is already on your bill
Slow service may reflect kitchen pace rather than your server's effort — context you have that math cannot account for

cases.name: gift-budget-supplied
cases.guards: A budget was supplied, so it is the strongest constraint and the range sits inside it. No single correct amount, and no claim about what the recipient expects or will spend.

why_this_range: Your stated budget is $150, so the range sits at or below that ceiling.
A cousin is a closer family relationship than a friend or colleague, which often — though not always — nudges gift amounts toward the higher end of whatever someone is comfortable spending.
The lower end of the range ($100) gives you a comfortable margin below your budget if you want to keep some flex.
output.budget_check: The full range fits within your $150 budget. Spending at the top of the range means you are at your stated limit, which is fine — that is what a budget ceiling is for.
output.social_context: What counts as an appropriate wedding gift for a cousin varies considerably by region, family culture, and the specific relationship. There is no universal standard. The most reliable signal is what feels right given your own means and how close you are — not an external benchmark.
output.if_you_want_to_spend_less: A gift in the $75–$99 range is still a real and considered gift, especially if you pair it with something personal — a handwritten card, a specific item from their registry that you know they care about, or something that reflects your relationship with them.
output.if_you_want_to_spend_more: Going above $150 primarily means a larger cash or registry contribution; for a cousin you are close to, that extra amount can meaningfully cover something on their registry they might not otherwise receive.

cases.name: salary-no-target-supplied
cases.guards: The recruiting case, and the twelve leaps the 2026-09-04 pass removed. No target figure was supplied, so ask.amount MUST be empty. Being recruited is CONTEXT, not leverage — 'the company initiated the recruiting conversation', never 'recruited, not applying, which shifts the starting posture'. Remote is not a financial benefit unless the visitor made that comparison. Tenure is not institutional knowledge or reduced ramp time at a different company. A belief that pay is below market does not make current salary a floor. No invented headcount or revenue milestone as promotion criteria. Unquantified equity is 'difficult to evaluate', never 'means nothing'. No equity upside asserted. Market data is evidence, never the correct salary. Every if_they_push_back entry is labelled as a possibility, never as what this employer will do. A script may not claim research the visitor never said they did — it must be conditional on verifying a figure first. And no named compensation-data provider, because their current relevance is unverified.

input.situation: A startup recruiter reached out about a Senior Marketing Manager role, fully remote, with a director track mentioned and broader ownership. My current role is hybrid three days a week. I think I am underpaid for my market.
input.experience: 6 years B2B SaaS marketing, 4 at current company

what_you_have_to_work_with: The company initiated the recruiting conversation — you did not apply
Six years of B2B SaaS marketing experience, including four years at your current company
The new role is fully remote; your current role is hybrid three days a week
A director track and broader ownership were mentioned by the recruiter
what_you_still_need_to_know: What base, bonus structure, and equity the company is offering or budgeting
What the director track actually means at this company — who decides, what needs to happen, and whether any timeline or review point is defined
Equity terms: type, amount, vesting schedule, strike price if options — difficult to evaluate without the actual details

Current compensation data for Senior Marketing Manager roles at comparable company stage, remote or your location, and industry — worth checking against more than one credible source before naming a number

ask.basis: You have not supplied a target figure, so no number is produced here. Once you have checked current compensation data for comparable roles — remote, B2B SaaS, similar company stage — you will have a defensible basis for an ask. Your current base of $115,000 is a data point, but if you believe it is below market, the market figure is what anchors your ask, not the current salary.
ask.script: Once you have verified a defensible figure, you could say: 'Based on what I have found for Senior Marketing Manager roles at this stage and scope — fully remote, B2B SaaS — and the broader ownership this role carries, I am looking for a base in the range of [figure you have researched and can support]. I also want to make sure I understand the full package, including bonus structure and equity terms, before we finalize anything. I am genuinely interested in the role and want to find something that works for both sides.'

if_they_push_back.situation: If they ask for your number before you have shared one
if_they_push_back.response: 'I want to make sure I have a complete picture of the role and the full package before I name a number — can you share what range you are working with, or what you had in mind for this level?'

if_they_push_back.situation: If the base they offer is lower than your researched figure
if_they_push_back.response: 'I appreciate the offer. Based on the scope of this role and what I have seen for comparable positions, I was expecting to be closer to [your figure] on base. Is there room to move on that, or flexibility elsewhere in the package?'

if_they_push_back.situation: If they point to equity as a reason to accept a lower base
if_they_push_back.response: 'I want to evaluate the equity seriously, and to do that I need to understand the terms — type, amount, vesting, and current valuation. Once I have those details I can look at the full picture together.'

if_they_push_back.situation: If they emphasize startup size or early-stage risk as context for the offer
if_they_push_back.response: 'I understand the stage, and that is part of why the equity terms matter to me. On base, I want to land somewhere I can support with the scope of the role and current data for comparable positions.'

other_terms_you_may_want_to_raise: The director track: what it requires, who decides, and whether any formal review point is defined — the recruiter raised it, so it is fair to ask for specifics
Bonus structure: target percentage, how it is measured, and how it has paid out recently
Equity: full terms before you can evaluate it alongside base and bonus
Remote setup: whether there is any equipment or home-office support — optional to raise, not something you mentioned as a priority

cases.name: family-no-dynamic-supplied
cases.guards: No family dynamic and no cultural context supplied. Nothing may infer guilt, obligation, favouritism, control or a 'real issue underneath the money' — the retired fields the_real_issue, emotional_stakes and if_guilt_trip must not reappear under any name. recommendation on THIS route is free prose, not an enum — it was coming back as 'Not enough to tell' because pinEnums ran globally on a field name Lending also uses, and the corrupted value was recorded into this golden. If it ever reads like one of Lending's four verdicts again, the pinner has lost its scope.

input.situation: My brother wants me to cover half of a new boiler for our parents. I can manage about a third.

output.practical_issue: Your brother is asking you to split the boiler cost equally, but you can only contribute a third. The gap between what he expects and what you can offer needs to be negotiated.
what_is_known: Your brother wants you to cover half the boiler cost
You can manage roughly a third of the cost
The boiler is for your parents
what_needs_clarifying: What is the total cost of the boiler, so the actual amounts are clear
Is there a third party — another sibling, parent savings, a grant — who could cover the remaining gap
What is the timeline for payment
Has any contribution amount been promised to your parents yet
output.recommendation: Tell your brother directly that a third is what you can commit to, and propose that you work out together how the remainder gets covered — whether by him, your parents, or another source.

conversation.opener: I want to help with the boiler — I can put in a third of the cost. I know that is not the half you were thinking, so let us figure out how to handle the difference.
key_points: Name your actual number once the total is confirmed: 'My share would be [a third of the total]'
Be clear this is your firm ceiling, not an opening position
Ask whether there is any other way to cover the shortfall before assuming he absorbs it alone
conversation.boundary_if_needed: A third is genuinely what I can do. I am not in a position to commit to more, and I do not want to promise something I cannot follow through on.
conversation.if_they_disagree: I understand that leaves a gap. I am open to problem-solving on how to close it, but the amount I can put in stays the same — a third is my limit.

cases.name: date-second-date
cases.guards: what_splitting_signals is gone. Nothing may say what any option signals about interest, independence, generosity, commitment or gender expectations — how_each_option_may_feel_or_function is conditional and about the evening, not the people. No confidence percentage.

input.situation: Second date, they suggested the restaurant

options.how_it_works: At the end of the meal, one of you picks up the check without discussion. Either you offer, or you wait to see if they do.
options.how_each_option_may_feel_or_function: This may feel simple and low-friction for the evening. If the other person was planning to contribute, it could prompt a brief back-and-forth about accepting or declining — which may or may not feel comfortable depending on how the date is going.
options.script: I have got this one — you can get the next one if you like.

options.how_it_works: When the check arrives, you suggest splitting it down the middle regardless of what each of you ordered.
options.how_each_option_may_feel_or_function: This keeps the arithmetic simple and avoids any ambiguity about who owes what. If one of you ordered significantly more or less, it may feel slightly uneven in practice — though this is only worth noting if the difference is large.
options.script: Want to just split it down the middle?

options.how_it_works: One of you covers this dinner with the understanding that the other will cover a future one. This works best if you say it out loud so both of you are on the same page.
options.how_each_option_may_feel_or_function: This spreads the cost across time rather than across a single bill. It does require both people to remember and follow through — so it may work better if stated clearly than if assumed.
options.script: I will grab this one — you can take the next one.

options.how_it_works: Before you look at the menu, briefly settle how you plan to handle the bill so neither of you is guessing at the end.
options.how_each_option_may_feel_or_function: Resolving this early removes any end-of-meal uncertainty, though some people find raising it at the start of a date slightly abrupt. Whether that fits the tone depends on how the conversation is flowing.
options.script: Just so we are not figuring it out at the end — want to split, or do something else?

what_you_told_me: The other person suggested the restaurant.
what_is_not_established: What the other person expects or prefers around who pays.
Whether either of you has a cultural or personal norm about this.
Whether the other person suggesting the restaurant implies any expectation about payment.
output.if_it_comes_up_awkwardly: If the check lands and neither of you has moved, a plain offer works fine: 'Want to split it, or do you want to handle it one way or the other?' That opens it without pressure.

cases.name: cultural-two-backgrounds
cases.guards: The hardest case. Neither background establishes an expectation. Nothing may describe Korea, the US, or any culture as having one money rule, say what an action 'actually means in their culture', or output a culture-clash score. Only expectations the visitor actually described may appear in what_you_have_described.

input.situation: His parents are visiting and want to take us out to dinner. I usually offer to split.

what_you_have_described: You typically offer to split the bill when dining out
Your partner's parents have invited you both to dinner
output.possible_mismatch: You have described your own default (offer to split), but you have not described what your partner or his parents expect when they extend an invitation. Those expectations may or may not align with yours.
what_not_to_assume: Growing up in Seoul does not tell you what this family expects around hosting and bills
Extending an invitation does not by itself establish whether they expect to pay entirely or welcome a split
Your partner's expectations are not known from his background alone
Your usual offer to split may or may not feel appropriate to them — you have not yet found out
questions_to_make_explicit: Ask your partner: when your parents invite us out, do they expect to treat us, or is splitting welcome?
Ask your partner: would offering to split feel polite to them, or could it come across differently?
Ask yourself: if they decline your offer, are you comfortable letting them pay without pressing further?
output.bridge: Check with your partner before the dinner so you are acting together rather than improvising at the table. Whatever their expectation turns out to be, a warm thank-you is always appropriate.
output.script: Hey, your parents are so kind to invite us. I want to handle the bill moment well — when they take us out, do they prefer to treat us, or would it feel natural if I offered to contribute? I just want to be respectful of what feels right to them.

cases.name: charity-tax-question
cases.guards: tax_note must say only that treatment depends on jurisdiction and recipient status and should be verified. No deductibility claim of any kind. recommendation here is free prose too, for the same reason — see the family case.

input.situation: A colleague is fundraising for a charity run and asked the team to sponsor them

output.recommendation: Give something small if you are comfortable doing so, or decline politely — either is reasonable for a colleague fundraiser. You are not obligated to contribute.
why: A peer fundraiser from a colleague carries mild social weight but no professional obligation.
The amount matters less than whether you feel comfortable giving at all.
Giving a token amount lets you participate without strain; a polite decline is also entirely normal in this context.
output.amount_guidance: For a colleague relationship, a small gesture — whatever feels negligible to you personally, often somewhere in the range of a coffee to a modest lunch — is typical. Pick a figure you would not think about again after giving it. Nothing about this situation requires generosity beyond your comfort level.
output.tax_note: Tax treatment depends on jurisdiction and the recipient's status; verify before relying on a deduction.
output.script: I am happy to sponsor you — great that you are doing this. I will keep it modest but wanted to show support. Good luck on the day!
output.if_they_push: I have already given what works for me right now, but I hope the run goes well. Thanks for understanding.

cases.name: inheritance-split-question
cases.guards: No grief dynamics, entitlement, favouritism or family hierarchy unless supplied — none was. No jurisdiction-specific legal or tax conclusion: those belong in needs_professional_confirmation. It must not decide that equal or equitable is objectively correct.

input.situation: Three of us are dividing our mother house. One sibling lived there and cared for her for the last two years.

output.arrangement_considered: Three siblings are dividing their mother's house. One sibling lived there and provided care for the last two years, which may affect how the three consider splitting the proceeds or ownership.

principles_in_tension.pulls_toward: Each sibling receives one third of the estate regardless of circumstances
The sibling who provided care and housing receives a larger share or separate compensation before the remainder is divided
Whatever the will specifies, if anything, takes precedence over informal arrangements

facts_that_matter: Whether the will addresses the caregiving sibling's share or living arrangement explicitly
Whether any written or witnessed agreement was made about compensation for care or rent-free occupancy
Whether the caregiving sibling paid expenses such as property tax, maintenance, or mortgage during the two years
Whether the caregiving sibling is still living in the house and needs time or a buyout arrangement to relocate
The current market value of the house, since the dollar difference between equal and adjusted splits depends on it
needs_professional_confirmation: What the will actually directs — only the executor and a solicitor can confirm the legal distribution
Whether a caregiver contribution claim or informal agreement has any legal standing in your jurisdiction
Tax implications of each sibling's share, particularly if one sibling buys the others out
Whether the estate must go through probate before the house can be sold or transferred

conversation.opener: Raise it as a question rather than a position: 'Before we decide how to divide things, I think we should talk about what the two years of care and living arrangement means for how we split it — does anyone have thoughts on that?'
what_to_clarify: Did Mum leave any written instructions or express wishes about the caregiving sibling's share?
Was there any agreement, even informal, about compensation or a larger share in exchange for the care provided?
Does the sibling who lived there need to stay in the house, or are they open to a sale or buyout?
Are all three siblings willing to get a professional valuation before deciding on numbers?
